title: Operate, Diagnose & Tear Down with Confidence
subtitle: Use job IDs, logs, service events and metrics to explain failures, then clean up every lab resource deliberately.
analogy: A useful runbook is a map from a visible symptom to evidence. Logs tell a story, metrics show patterns, and a shell is an investigative tool—not the first fix for every alert.
objectives: Follow a failed request or job across the system.
Distinguish container, host, network and data failures.
Create an alert and confirm its notification destination.
Review destruction and verify both IaC and manual resources afterward.
prerequisites: A deployed lab with logs and at least one completed job.
The Session Manager plugin is needed for interactive ECS Exec/SSM commands. Install it for your platform using the official guide.

lessons.title: Start with evidence, not restarts
body: For HTTP failures, check ALB target health, API logs and database reachability. For missing results, keep the returned job_id, inspect worker logs and queue-consumer state, and query PostgreSQL. A healthy /health endpoint does not prove background processing works.
Correlate timestamps and stable job IDs across logs. Do not log credentials or full sensitive prompts. The lab’s completion log records the ID and count only.

lessons.title: Container shell versus host session
body: ECS Exec enters a running container using the task role’s ssmmessages permissions and a caller authorized to execute-command. Enabling Exec affects newly launched tasks, not existing tasks retroactively.

SSM start-session enters an EC2 host using its SSM agent/profile and the caller’s session permissions. Fargate exposes no host shell. Grant and audit interactive access deliberately; never open port 22 just to make a shell work.

lessons.title: An alarm needs a delivery path
body: The example alerts when ALB target 5xx count exceeds 5 in each of two one-minute evaluation periods. It uses notBreaching for missing data; low traffic therefore does not itself alarm. This metric does not cover queue backlog or every ALB-generated error.

Create and confirm an SNS subscription and test delivery. A configured topic with no confirmed subscriber does not notify a human. A production runbook should connect alerts to a clear owner and response action.

lessons.title: Destruction is a data decision
body: Terraform destroy removes only resources in this state, not manually created stacks. The lab allows deleting database data without a final snapshot and deleting ECR images; do not copy those choices to data you need to retain.

Inspect the destroy plan, take any required backups, and keep the separate state bucket until recovery/audit needs are resolved. NAT Elastic IPs, snapshots, retained logs, untracked resources and separate manual labs can continue incurring charges.

handHoldingSteps: Copy infra/08-alarms.tf, review/apply the plan and subscribe a real address to the SNS topic. Confirm the subscription before assuming alerts work.
List tasks and inspect stopped reasons/service events before opening a shell. Follow CloudWatch logs and correlate a job_id across API acceptance and worker completion.
Use ECS Exec only when needed. If operating the optional EC2 worker, use SSM for host inspection; a host shell and a container shell show different process/network contexts.
Verify rollback behavior with a deliberately bad image/health configuration in the isolated lab. Keep a known-good SHA and a database-compatible recovery plan.
Review a saved destroy plan using the preserved input settings and the correct account. Apply only after deciding whether database/cache data must be retained.

Verify state is empty, inspect project-tagged resources and manually inspect the earlier bootcamp-manual stack. Remove local Compose resources separately; retain or deliberately clean up the separate state bucket.
concepts: Logs vs metrics: Logs explain individual events; metrics and alarms identify patterns that deserve investigation.
Container vs host: ECS Exec and SSM enter different execution environments and use different permissions.
Teardown scope: Empty Terraform state does not prove that the AWS account contains no billable resources.

commands.command:
CLUSTER=$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw cluster_name)
aws ecs describe-services --cluster "$CLUSTER" --services bootcamp-iac-api
aws logs tail /ecs/bootcamp-iac --since 10m --follow
commands.explanation: Inspect service events and recent logs. Ctrl+C stops following logs without stopping services.
commands.expected: Useful startup, deployment or completion evidence.

commands.command:
TASK_ARN=$(aws ecs list-tasks --cluster "$CLUSTER" --service-name bootcamp-iac-api --query 'taskArns[0]' --output text)
aws ecs execute-command --cluster "$CLUSTER" --task "$TASK_ARN" --container api --interactive --command /bin/sh
commands.explanation: Requires Session Manager plugin, Exec enabled on the task, suitable caller permissions and running SSM channels. Avoid printing the whole environment because it includes a password.
commands.expected: A shell inside the API container; exit returns to your local terminal.

commands.command:
INSTANCE_ID=$(aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:aws:autoscaling:groupName,Values=bootcamp-iac-hosts Name=instance-state-name,Values=running --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].InstanceId' --output text)
aws ssm start-session --target "$INSTANCE_ID"
commands.explanation: Only for worker_on_ec2=true and a registered SSM-managed host. Inside the host, inspect sudo docker ps.
commands.expected: An EC2 host session, not a Fargate host session.

commands.command:
TOPIC_ARN=$(terraform -chdir=infra output -raw alerts_topic_arn)
aws sns subscribe --topic-arn "$TOPIC_ARN" --protocol email --notification-endpoint YOUR_EMAIL
# Confirm the email link, then test delivery:
aws sns publish --topic-arn "$TOPIC_ARN" --message "Bootcamp test notification"
commands.explanation: Replace YOUR_EMAIL and confirm the subscription; check delivery before relying on the alarm.
commands.expected: A confirmed subscriber receives the test message.

commands.command:
aws sts get-caller-identity
terraform -chdir=infra plan -destroy -out=destroy.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra show destroy.tfplan
# After reviewing backups, account and resource scope:
terraform -chdir=infra apply destroy.tfplan
terraform -chdir=infra state list
commands.explanation: The preserved auto.tfvars file also supplies the required OIDC input if Chapter 9 is installed. Review before applying: this lab deletes its database without a final snapshot.
commands.expected: State list is empty after successful destruction.

commands.command:
aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=Project,Values=bootcamp-iac
aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter Name=state,Values=available
aws ec2 describe-addresses
aws rds describe-db-instances
docker compose down
commands.explanation: Read-only post-destroy inspection; not every resource type appears in the tagging API. Separately remove manual lab resources and review any retained snapshots/logs/state bucket.
commands.expected: No unintended lab resources remain; local volumes persist unless deliberately removed.

codeFiles.description: A symptom-based alarm and SNS destination; the email subscription is a separate deliberate step.

walkthrough.title: Metric dimensions
walkthrough.explanation: LoadBalancer uses the ALB ARN suffix, not its full ARN. The target-5xx metric describes errors returned by application targets.

walkthrough.title: Evaluation and missing data
walkthrough.explanation: Two one-minute evaluation periods reduce reaction to isolated errors. notBreaching avoids treating absent traffic as application failure.

walkthrough.title: Delivery
walkthrough.explanation: alarm_actions targets SNS. Subscribe and confirm a destination; the topic alone does not deliver email.

breakItDrill.title: Prove notification delivery
breakItDrill.scenario: Publish a test message before confirming the email subscription.
breakItDrill.symptom: The topic exists but no confirmed destination receives the message.
breakItDrill.fix: Confirm the subscription, publish again and document the delivered message.

assignment.title: Create your operations runbook
assignment.description: Write separate procedures for API 503, accepted-but-unfinished jobs, unhealthy targets, failed secret injection and safe teardown. Include commands, expected evidence and a verification step for each.
assignment.completionHint: Verify the result yourself, then complete the chapter checklist.

recallNote.keyTakeaway: An operation is complete when the user-visible path works and the evidence confirms why.
bullets: Use stable job IDs for correlation.
An alarm without a confirmed subscriber is incomplete.
ECS Exec enters a container; SSM enters an EC2 host.
Destroy only removes managed objects in the selected state.

checklist.text: Follow a failed request or job across the system.
Distinguish container, host, network and data failures.
Create an alert and confirm its notification destination.
Review destruction and verify both IaC and manual resources afterward.
